answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud is proven. Creating a hundred fake identities does not multiply influence for free: each one needs capital, and coordinated Sybils risk losing it all. The stake is not proof of a unique human, but it makes attacks costly; meadow, saffron, and sable can name test agents without changing that mechanism.
